Motivation

test/registered/attention/test_verify_shared_kv.py::test_qwen3_5_fp8_kv_cache has never passed on stage-b-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x since it was added (#34517); it fails inside the Triton AMD backend, not in sglang code (latest instance):

python3: llvm/ADT/SmallVector.h:292: Assertion `idx < size()' failed.
extend_attention.py:305:0: error: Failures have been detected while processing an MLIR pass pipeline
extend_attention.py:305:0: note: Pipeline failed while executing [`ConvertTritonAMDGPUToLLVM` ...]
RuntimeError: PassManager::run failed

Only the fp8 variant fails; the bf16 variants of the same test pass. The crash is not test-specific — it is in the shared prefill kernel, so a model served on MI35x with --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 through the Triton attention backend hits it, in decode as well as prefill. (Backends that do not route through these kernels, and the two ROCm Triton kernels that cannot take an fp8 pool at all, are out of scope; see Modifications.)

Scope: the ROCm 7.0 image only — 7.2 was never affected. The dividing line is the Triton wheel, not ROCm. On the pre-fix ROCm 7.2 MI35x lane (job 95705686213, Aug 18, before any commit here) test_verify_shared_kv.py reported "passed": true with no PassManager::run failed or idx < size() in the log; that lane's only red was the unrelated test_quark_mxfp4.py near-miss. The 7.0 log carries aiter's require triton>=3.6.0, found 3.4.0, while 7.2 emits no such warning, so its Triton clears 3.6.0 (docker/rocm.Dockerfile installs aiter's pin over the base ROCm Torch triton==3.5.1 when BUILD_TRITON=1).

Root cause

Every Triton attention kernel that reads a KV pool casts the wide operand down to the pool dtype before the dot (tl.dot(q.to(k.dtype), k), tl.dot(p.to(v.dtype), v)), so an fp8 pool also feeds the fp8 matrix core. On gfx950 AccelerateAMDMatmul promotes an fp8 x fp8 tl.dot to the scaled V_MFMA_*_F8F6F4 family, which is 16x16x128 under the matrix_instr_nonkdim=16 launch hint all of these kernels pass.

A dot whose reduction is narrower than 128 does not tile that instruction: AMDMfmaEncodingAttr::getRepForOperand clamps the resulting zero K-repetitions up to one, and ScaledDotOpMFMAConversionHelper then reads kBase = 32 elements per lane from a register range that only holds K / 4. That is the out-of-bounds SmallVector access.

P @ V reduces BLOCK_N, which is 64 (extend, verify) or 32 (decode, split-KV verify) — never 128 — so the fp8 path never compiles on gfx950. Q @ Kpe reduces BLOCK_DPE (32/64) and Q @ K reduces BLOCK_DMODEL, which is also below 128 at head_dim <= 64.

Triton rejects the intrinsic instead of miscompiling it as of triton-lang/triton#8278, which dropped the enforcedNonKDim == 0 && escape hatch that had let an explicit matrix_instr_nonkdim skip Triton's own "K is not a multiple of the intrinsic's kDim" check. That fix missed 3.5 and landed in 3.6:

Triton branch guard in chooseMfmaInstruction narrow fp8 dot
release/3.4.x, release/3.5.x enforcedNonKDim == 0 && inputKSize % kDim != 0 promoted, then aborts
release/3.6.x and later if (inputKSize % kDim != 0) rejected, falls back to non-scaled fp8 MFMA

So anything on 3.4 or 3.5 with matrix_instr_nonkdim set — which is every kernel here — crashes, and the ROCm 7.0 image ships 3.4.0.

The guard therefore carries a triton.__version__ < 3.6 term, so it is inert on 7.2. Without it the guard also fired on 7.2, where Triton already falls back to the non-scaled V_MFMA_F32_16X16X32_FP8_FP8 and the narrow dot works — the same pre-fix job ran test_qwen3_5_fp8_kv_cache green. That would have substituted a bf16 dot for a working fp8 one on the lane that gates PRs, trading unquantized P (more accurate) against fp8→bf16 converts and a 2-byte V tile in LDS, for a rate difference nobody has measured. Not a trade worth making on the primary lane.

With the version term:

  • 7.0 / Triton 3.4 — guard active, replaces a hard compile abort.
  • 7.2 / Triton ≥3.6 — guard inert, codegen byte-identical to today.
  • When ROCm 7.0 is dropped the guard is permanently inert and the whole module can be deleted, so this does not become long-lived debt.

extend_attention.py already gates gfx950 tile choices on _is_triton_ge_37, so a Triton-version term is an established idiom in this file rather than a new mechanism. A version string that will not parse keeps the guard on, which is the safe direction.

Modifications

  • New python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/fp8_dot_support.py with dot_in_kv_dtype(kv_dtype, reduction_width): True for every non-fp8 pool and every arch other than gfx950, and on gfx950 only for reduction widths that tile the scaled MFMA instruction.
  • Each dot that casts an operand down to the tile it reads gets its own constexpr verdict (QK_DOT_IN_KV_DTYPE, QK_PE_DOT_IN_KV_DTYPE, PV_DOT_IN_KV_DTYPE, PV_EXTEND_DOT_IN_V_DTYPE). When it is False the KV tile is upcast to the query dtype instead of the query tile being cast down. This covers _fwd_kernel and _fwd_kernel_unified (extend), _fwd_grouped_kernel_stage1 (decode), _verify_mla_prefix_stage1, and _verify_prefix_stage1 — including _fwd_kernel's extend-stage P @ V, whose V is the caller's current-chunk tensor rather than the pool.
    Every flag is True on non-gfx950 hardware and for bf16/fp16 pools, so those paths generate the same code as before. matrix_instr_nonkdim, tile sizes, warp counts, and the #mma layout are all untouched.

Non-AMD impact: none, verified rather than argued. is_gfx95_supported() returns False for every non-HIP build without touching the device, so dot_in_kv_dtype short-circuits to True on NVIDIA and the guards select the pre-existing expression. To confirm that costs nothing, I compiled the original kernel body and the guarded one (flags True) for five targets with Triton 3.4.0 and diffed the emitted TTGIR and LLIR modulo debug locations: identical on sm90 (bf16 and fp8), sm100 (fp8), gfx942 (fp8) and gfx950 (bf16). That check is what caught the one real difference — writing the guard as tl.dot(p.to(v.dtype), v) reorders the P cast against the acc * re_scale multiply, which on Hopper with an fp8 pool moved the async warp_group_dot relative to the accumulator scaling. Keeping p = p.to(v.dtype) as its own statement inside the guard restores exact equivalence, which is why it is written that way. NVIDIA fp8 KV keeps casting down to fp8 and keeps its fp8 tensor-core path. The residual cost off gfx950 is one extra Triton compile (the new constexpr parameters change the cache key) and three or four integer / frozenset comparisons per launch.

Two other ROCm Triton kernels dot against a tile that could in principle be fp8, and deliberately get no verdict:

  • prefill_attention.py never reads a KV pool, its Q @ K is uncast (so its operands already share a dtype), and its gfx950 BLOCK_N is 128 — which tiles the scaled instruction even if P @ V ran in fp8.
  • rocm_mla_decode_rope.py does read the pool, but its Q @ K is uncast too, so a bf16 query against an fp8 pool fails Triton's frontend with Unsupported rhs dtype fp8e4nv well before the AMD backend. That is a separate pre-existing gap in that kernel, not this crash, and a per-dot verdict would not make it work.

The verify combine kernels compute their draft-draft block with tl.sum(q[:, None, :] * ke[None, :, :], 2), not tl.dot, so no matrix-core promotion applies there.

On unit tests: I wrote and then dropped a CPU test for the predicate. Asserting dot_in_kv_dtype(fp8, 64) is False against a body of width % 128 == 0 only restates the expression, and the one assertion with real coupling — that the gfx950 head_dim-256 config yields a BLOCK_N the guard rejects — would fail if someone legitimately retuned BLOCK_N to 128, which is the documented fallback here. Pinning that would block an improvement rather than catch a bug. The failure mode worth guarding is "a new narrow fp8 dot appears on gfx950", and what catches that is compiling the real kernel on real gfx950, i.e. the MI35x lane.

Alternatives considered and rejected: dropping or raising matrix_instr_nonkdim for the fp8 path (Triton's own guard then rejects the intrinsic, but the 16x16 tile becomes 32x32, which changes warpsPerTile for the chain-dot tail from [8, 1] to [4, 2] and inserts a layout conversion between the two dots), and forcing BLOCK_N = 128 (fixes only head_dim 256 and re-tunes the bf16 path with it).

Accuracy Tests

stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x now passes on MI35x hardware. Run 32217006660 is a targeted dispatch of just that stage against this PR's head (ROCm 7.0, since that lane is schedule-only and a PR event never runs it): 9/9 passed, test_verify_shared_kv.py reports "passed": true with test_qwen3_5_fp8_kv_cache executing, and the log contains no PassManager::run failed or idx < size(). (Run 32212523645 is the same result on the first commit.)

The change only affects gfx950 with an fp8 KV pool, where nothing compiled before, so there is no prior behaviour to regress. Within that path P reaches the dot as bf16 rather than quantized to e4m3, which is strictly more accurate; extend_attention_fwd and verify_shared_kv_fwd widen the same dots, so test_qwen3_5_fp8_kv_cache's parity check compares like with like.

Speed Tests and Profiling

@chuyeh benched the three #34517 kernels on MI355X at the Qwen3.5 TP4-local verify shape (full tables). fp8 pool versus bf16 pool at a 16k prefix:

Kernel bf16 pool fp8 pool Δ
grouped-head verify 0.048 ms 0.042 ms −12%
split-KV verify 0.073 ms 0.056 ms −23%
extend 1.069 ms 1.791 ms +68%

The bandwidth-bound verify kernels gain from the halved KV traffic; extend regresses. Two caveats on reading that:

  1. Those numbers are from 780d4ab, before the Triton-version term. On ROCm 7.2 the guard was still firing there, so the fp8 extend row is the widened bf16 P @ V. At HEAD the guard is inert on 7.2, so that row should not reproduce on that image.
  2. The bench cannot attribute the +68%. A pool that halves KV bytes made the other two kernels faster, so extend moving the other way is either the widened P @ V (fp8→bf16 V converts plus a 2-byte V tile in LDS, paid every iteration of a serial prefix loop at BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=64/head_dim 256) or something inherent to fp8 extend that this PR neither causes nor cures. An extend-only rerun at HEAD on 7.2 separates them; requested, not blocking.

What this does not change: on ROCm 7.0 the alternative to widening is a compile abort, so a slower extend is still the right trade there, and it is the only image that pays it. If the widening does own the regression, the follow-up lever is BLOCK_N = 128 for the fp8 extend tile — it reaches the scaled 16x16x128 instruction on both dots and compiles today, at the cost of retuning the tile and doubling the K/V LDS footprint. That belongs in its own change with numbers behind it, not here.

Independently useful from the same run: "the flags-True path does not move the bf16 numbers", which confirms the codegen-equivalence check above on hardware.

Verification

Triton 3.4.0's AMD backend compiles for hip:gfx950 without a GPU, so the fix was checked by driving the ttir/ttgir/llir stages directly on the same tile shape and launch hints as extend_attention at head_dim 256 (BLOCK_M=128, num_warps=8, matrix_instr_nonkdim=16):

KV dtype PV_DOT_IN_KV_DTYPE BLOCK_N Result
fp8_e4m3 True (today) 64 RuntimeError: PassManager::run failed
fp8_e4m3 False (this PR) 64 compiles
fp8_e4m3 True 32 Assertion 'idx < size()' failed
fp8_e4m3 False 32 compiles
fp8_e4m3 True 128 compiles (128 tiles the instruction)
bf16 True 64 compiles (unchanged path)

The fixed variant's TTGIR keeps the fp8 fast path where it is legal and drops to bf16 only for P @ V, both under the same #mma layout as before:

%50 = tt.dot_scaled %28, %49, %cst_2 lhs = e4m3 rhs = e4m3 : tensor<128x256xf8E4M3FN, dot_op<{opIdx = 0, parent = #mma, kWidth = 16}>> * tensor<256x64xf8E4M3FN, ...>
%77 = tt.dot %76, %75, %73 : tensor<128x64xbf16, dot_op<{opIdx = 0, parent = #mma, kWidth = 4}>> * tensor<64x256xbf16, dot_op<{opIdx = 1, parent = #mma, kWidth = 4}>>

The K3 MLA tile (BLOCK_DMODEL=512, BLOCK_DPE=64, BLOCK_N=64), where two of the three dots widen, behaves the same way: crashes today, compiles with the per-dot verdicts. Narrowing BLOCK_DMODEL to 64 crashes the Q @ K dot too, which is why the verdict is computed per dot rather than assuming Q @ K is always wide enough.

Checklist

  • Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit.
  • Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests. The regression test is the existing test_verify_shared_kv.py::test_qwen3_5_fp8_kv_cache on stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x, which this PR turns green; no new test file is added (see below).
  • Update documentation according to Write documentations.
  • Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to Test the accuracy and Benchmark the speed.
  • Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

2252a2d 
Every Triton attention kernel that reads a KV pool casts the wide operand
down to the pool dtype before the dot, so an fp8 pool also feeds the fp8

P @ V always reduces BLOCK_N (32 or 64), so an fp8 KV cache on MI35x fails
to compile in extend, decode, and both verify kernels. Give each pool-reading
dot a constexpr verdict on whether it may run in the pool dtype, and upcast

non-scaled fp8 MFMA reduces as many elements per instruction as bf16.

P @ V reduces BLOCK_N — 64 here, 32 in decode — which does not tile it, so getRepForOperand clamps zero K-repetitions up to one and the AMD backend then reads 32 elements per lane out of a range holding K / 4, aborting with PassManager::run failed. Review follow-up. The extend stage's P @ V casts P down to the current
chunk's V dtype, the same pattern that crashes gfx950 when the reduction is
narrower than the scaled MFMA instruction. Callers pass the chunk in the
query dtype today, so the verdict is True in practice, but the dot is now
guarded on v_extend rather than assuming that.

possibly-fp8 tile need no verdict: prefill_attention never reads a KV pool,
has an uncast Q @ K, and uses BLOCK_N=128 on gfx950, which tiles the scaled

rhs dtype fp8e4nv" before the AMD backend sees it.

Nit — you were right about one of the three, and I covered it.

_fwd_kernel's extend-stage P @ V on V_Extend is the same cast-down pattern with the same BLOCK_N reduction, so it now carries its own verdict (PV_EXTEND_DOT_IN_V_DTYPE) keyed on v_extend.dtype. Every caller passes the chunk in the query dtype today — stage 2 applies sm_scale without k_scale, which makes that structural rather than incidental — so the flag is True in practice and codegen is unchanged. Guarding it is still right: it removes an unguarded narrow dot from the file the crash was reported in.

The other two I checked rather than patched, and the PR body now says so instead of claiming "any fp8 KV serve":

  • prefill_attention.py never reads a KV pool (callers pass the current chunk — extend_attention.py's no-prefix path and vision.py), its Q @ K is uncast so operands already share a dtype, and its gfx950 BLOCK_N is 128, which tiles V_MFMA_SCALE_F32_16X16X128_F8F6F4 exactly — so even an fp8 P @ V there is legal. I confirmed the 128 case compiles in the offline harness.
  • rocm_mla_decode_rope.py does read the pool, but qk += tl.dot(q, kv) is uncast, and q_input is built from bf16 q while kv comes from the pool. Triton's frontend rejects the mixed dot — I checked against 3.4.0 for hip:gfx950 and got AssertionError: Unsupported rhs dtype fp8e4nv — so it never reaches ConvertTritonAMDGPUToLLVM. That kernel simply cannot serve an fp8 pool today, which is a separate gap; a per-dot verdict on its P @ V would not fix it. Happy to file an issue if you want it tracked.

Also checked while I was in there: both verify combine kernels compute the draft-draft block with tl.sum(q[:, None, :] * ke[None, :, :], 2) rather than tl.dot, so no matrix-core promotion applies.

Perf. Agreed, and thank you — please do post the extend / split-KV / grouped-head verify numbers against an fp8 pool. I've marked my throughput argument as reasoning, not measurement, in the PR body. To make it falsifiable, what I'd expect you to see: Q @ K unchanged (it stays on tt.dot_scaled), and P @ V at bf16 MFMA rate, which on CDNA4 equals the non-scaled V_MFMA_F32_16X16X32_FP8_FP8 rate at the same 32 elements per instruction. The measurable cost is the fp8→bf16 converts on the V tile plus that tile's LDS footprint doubling (80 KB total at head_dim 256, versus 128 KB for a bf16 pool). If P @ V lands materially slower than that, BLOCK_N = 128 is the fallback — it compiles today with fp8 on both dots, at the cost of re-tuning the tile.

Triton bump. Understood — landing this first; an image bump can follow independently, since nothing here depends on the wheel version.

[AMD] Keep the guarded P @ V casts as their own statement
780d4ab 
Writing the guard as `tl.dot(p.to(v.dtype), v)`, or hoisting the dot into a
temporary, moves the P cast relative to the acc * re_scale broadcast-multiply,
so the flags-True path emitted the same ops in a different order rather than
byte-identical IR. On Hopper with an fp8 pool that reordered the async
warp_group_dot against the accumulator scaling.

Restoring the original standalone `p = p.to(v.dtype)` statement inside the
guard makes the True path reproduce the pre-change TTGIR and LLIR exactly.
Verified offline against Triton 3.4.0 for sm90 (bf16 and fp8), sm100 (fp8),
gfx942 (fp8) and gfx950 (bf16): identical on all five, while gfx950 with an
fp8 pool and BLOCK_N=64 still crashes unguarded and still compiles guarded.

@chuyeh thanks for confirming. The fp8-pool bench you offered is the one open item from your review, so whenever you have MI35x time: extend / split-KV / grouped-head verify latency from the #34517 bench against an fp8 pool, at HEAD 780d4ab versus a bf16 pool as the reference point.

Two notes on the run you cited, so the numbers land against the right baseline:

The red in run 32309790713 was test_quark_mxfp4.py, not the fp8 test — TestNVFP4ToMXFP4MOETP1.test_gsm8k, which sits on a 0.85 GSM8K gate. Across my three MI35x runs it drew 0.844→0.864 (passed on retry), 0.860 (passed), 0.820→0.844 (failed). The 0.844 appears on my first commit and my last, on both sides of the gate, so it's the near-miss cluster rather than anything here. The rerun is 9/9 green, test_verify_shared_kv.py included.

Since your review I also pushed 780d4ab, which only changes how the guard is written: keeping p = p.to(v.dtype) as its own statement instead of inlining it into tl.dot(...). That matters for your bench baseline — inlining reordered the P cast against the acc * re_scale multiply, which on Hopper with an fp8 pool moved the async warp_group_dot relative to the accumulator scaling. With the statement form, flags-True codegen is byte-identical to pre-change TTGIR/LLIR on sm90 (bf16 and fp8), sm100 (fp8), gfx942 (fp8) and gfx950 (bf16), verified by diffing against Triton 3.4.0. So a bf16-pool bench should be unchanged from main; if it isn't, that's a finding in itself.

What I expect you to see on the fp8 pool, stated so it's easy to falsify:

  • Q @ K unchanged — it stays on tt.dot_scaled at BLOCK_DMODEL 256/512.
  • P @ V at bf16 MFMA rate, which on CDNA4 is the same 32 elements per instruction as the non-scaled V_MFMA_F32_16X16X32_FP8_FP8 that a Triton carrying triton#8278 would fall back to. So no loss against a fixed-Triton baseline, though it is a loss against the scaled 16x16x128 path that a 128-wide reduction would reach.
  • Measurable overhead: fp8→bf16 converts on the V tile, plus that tile's LDS footprint doubling (80 KB total at head_dim 256 versus 128 KB for a bf16 pool).

If P @ V comes out materially slower than the bf16-pool reference, the fallback is BLOCK_N = 128: it compiles today with fp8 on both dots and reaches the scaled instruction, at the cost of re-tuning the tile and doubling the K/V tiles. I'd rather land the safe form now and take that as a follow-up with your numbers behind it than guess at the tile size.

For anyone triaging the board: the remaining reds are 11 base-c GPU jobs that a maintenance workflow cancelled (4 succeeded, 11 cancelled, 0 failed), the NPU/Xeon/XPU lanes, the two known AMD clusters (R352 hipblasCreate flake, R371 with fix #35364 open), and the two run-ci-extra-gated workflows I left off deliberately.

@michaelzhang-ai Numbers from the #34517 kernel bench against an fp8 pool, as requested.

Setup:

  1. MI355X, ROCm 7.2. Kernels from 780d4ab. Qwen3.5 TP4-local verify shape: 8 query heads sharing 1 KV head, head dim 256, 4 draft tokens, bs=1.
  2. Same three kernels as [AMD][Spec] Accelerate Qwen3.5 verification with grouped-head shared KV #34517: extend_attention_fwd, split-KV verify, grouped-head verify.
  3. bf16 pool as the reference, while fp8 e4m3 pool is the new path.

bf16 KV pool

Prefix Extend (ms) Split-KV (ms) Grouped-head (ms)
1,024 0.081 0.029 0.021
2,048 0.145 0.043 0.027
4,096 0.282 0.044 0.030
8,192 0.541 0.044 0.035
16,384 1.069 0.073 0.048

Matches the #34517 table within run-to-run noise. The flags-True path does not move the bf16 numbers.

fp8 e4m3 KV pool

Prefix Extend (ms) Split-KV (ms) Grouped-head (ms)
1,024 0.133 0.024 0.024
2,048 0.242 0.034 0.026
4,096 0.464 0.035 0.028
8,192 0.906 0.035 0.033
16,384 1.791 0.056 0.042

At 16k vs the bf16 pool: grouped-head −12% (0.048 → 0.042), split-KV −23% (0.073 → 0.056), extend +68% (1.069 → 1.791).

That matches the split you predicted: Q @ K stays on the scaled fp8 path, and the bandwidth-bound verify kernels pick up the smaller KV traffic. Extend is the one that pays for the widened P @ V (serial prefix loop, BLOCK_N=64). That is the “materially slower than the bf16-pool reference” case you called out, for extend, not for grouped-head / split-KV.

The fp8 path compiles and grouped-head / split-KV are faster than the bf16 pool. From my side, it's fine to land the current form.

[AMD] Gate the fp8 dot guard on Triton < 3.6
11c37a4 
triton-lang/triton#8278 landed in 3.6, so from there Triton rejects the scaled
intrinsic itself and falls back to the non-scaled fp8 MFMA -- the narrow dots
compile and stay in fp8. Only ROCm 7.0 (Triton 3.4.0) aborts; the ROCm 7.2
image ships >=3.6 and ran test_qwen3_5_fp8_kv_cache green before this branch.

Without the version term the guard also fired on 7.2, substituting a bf16 dot
for a working fp8 one on the lane that gates PRs, for an unmeasured perf
delta. With it, 7.2 codegen is byte-identical to today, the fix is confined to
the images that would otherwise crash, and the whole guard goes inert -- and
becomes deletable -- when ROCm 7.0 is dropped.

@chuyeh thank you — that's exactly the shape of data I couldn't get from here, and the extend row changes what I'd land.

Two things to flag, one of them a timing accident on my side.

Your bench predates the version gate. 780d4ab had no Triton-version term, so on ROCm 7.2 the guard was firing and your fp8 extend row is the widened bf16 P @ V. I pushed 11c37a4ba8 at 03:01, six minutes after your comment, gating the guard on triton.__version__ < 3.6 — precisely because 7.2 already falls back to the non-scaled V_MFMA_F32_16X16X32_FP8_FP8 on its own and shouldn't be perturbed. At current HEAD on 7.2 the guard is inert, so the extend +68% you measured should not reproduce there. Sorry for the moving target.

But your number may be measuring something worse than the guard, and it's worth knowing which. A pool that halves KV bytes made your two bandwidth-bound kernels faster (split-KV −23%, grouped-head −12%); extend going +68% the other way is not what a byte reduction alone does. Two candidates:

  1. the widened P @ V — the fp8→bf16 V converts plus the 2-byte V tile in LDS, paid every iteration of extend's serial prefix loop at BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=64/head_dim 256; or
  2. something inherent to fp8 extend independent of this PR.

Your table can't separate them, and it matters: (1) is fixed on 7.2 by 11c37a4ba8 and is a real cost we knowingly accept on 7.0, while (2) is a pre-existing perf bug this PR neither causes nor cures.

One row would settle it whenever convenient: extend only, fp8 pool, ROCm 7.2, at HEAD (11c37a4ba8) instead of 780d4ab. Guard inert there, so it isolates the widening. If extend lands near the bf16 1.069 ms, the cost is the widening and 7.0 is the only image paying it. If it stays near 1.791 ms, the widening is not the story and I'll open a separate issue for fp8 extend on gfx950.

Either way I'm not asking you to block on it — 11c37a4ba8 keeps 7.2 byte-identical to today, and on 7.0 the alternative to widening is a compile abort, so extend being slower there is still the right trade. If the widening does own the +68%, the follow-up lever is BLOCK_N = 128 for the fp8 extend tile: it reaches the scaled 16x16x128 instruction on both dots and compiles today, at the cost of retuning the tile and doubling K/V LDS. I'd rather do that as its own change with your numbers behind it.

Also useful, thank you: "the flags-True path does not move the bf16 numbers" independently confirms the codegen-equivalence check I ran offline.

MI35x is green at HEAD with the gate in place — run 32441920092, 9/9, test_verify_shared_kv.py included, no crash markers.
